diagnosis: Annex-D negotiated-procedure awards publish their justification as a @REASON attribute no rule claimed, so the whole award was held; REASON is now a captured attribute.
The RP authority code was scalar, but international-financing records list each co-financier on a continuation line; RP is now per-line, so every institution is kept.

The 1995-98 text vintages carry the main object CPV as OC (paired with the English description ON), which no rule claimed, quarantining the whole notice; OC is now claimed as CPV codes and ON as its description.

The 2008 OPOCE export is real S-series notices behind a DTD (INTERNAL_OJS R2.0.5) that roxmltree refused wholesale; the DTD is now safely stripped and the era is reclassified from a misleading parse error to a tracked unmapped-era (its parser is issue 41).

The INTERNAL_OJS R2.0.5 era (~28k opoce-only S-series notices, the whole 2008 coverage gap) had no mapping profile and was held as a tracked unmapped-era. It is now parsed by the internal-ojs profile: a new envelope reader for the BIB_INFO/BIB_DOC_S coded backbone plus an explicit _SUM alias shim that reuses the r209 walker for the 85%-shared form body. Reprocessing the bucket reclaims the era into notices.

eForms notices declaring an SDK version (1.0-1.11) whose fields.json we had not vendored were held whole as unknown-customization - by far the largest bucket. All versions are now vendored (1.8-1.11 directly; 1.0-1.7 also needed an xpath grammar extension for descendant-axis and boolean-or predicates plus a predicate-free BT-165 binding), and the reprocess mechanism reclaims each held notice from the archive in place. The recovery rebuild (ADR-0009) folds them into the tender layer.

German eForms-DE 1.0/1.1/1.2 notices were held as unknown-customization: the national 1.x line is spec-and-schematron only, with no published field metadata to parse against. The inventory was rebuilt empirically from the archived corpus (issue 75), with grafts for the DÖE serializer's inlined parties (issue 78), then the cohort was reclaimed and projected. These tenders now carry their German title and description, CPV, NUTS, lots, deadlines and estimated values, the buyer, and the other named organization roles — review body, information and document providers, tender recipient, evaluator, mediator. AWARD WINNERS ARE NOT RESOLVED for this dialect (issue 100): the result graph references sections by their published ids while those sections are keyed synthetically, so the LotResult → LotTender → TenderingParty chain does not link. Award notices therefore show their lots, contracts and awarded values, and bidders where a notice names them, but not which bidder won. That is a parse-layer defect: fixing it requires re-parsing the cohort, so it is deliberately not part of this batch. A residual ~241 notices remain held pending re-parse and still carry their original unknown-customization reason, which is now stale; they are tracked separately (issue 87).
